sources.entry: Svix - Webhooks as a service that makes it super easy for API providers to send webhooks. (Source Code) MIT Docker/Rust

summary.one_liner: Svix is an open-source webhook sending service: developers make one API call and the Svix server handles delivery, retries, and signing of outgoing webhooks.
summary.what_it_does: The repository contains the Svix server (written in Rust), which dispatches webhook messages to customer endpoints. It stores events in PostgreSQL and can use Redis or Valkey for its task queue and cache. Messages are signed before sending, using symmetric (pre-shared key) signatures by default or asymmetric ed25519 keys as an option. Access to the API is controlled by JWTs signed with a configurable secret and algorithm. The README also covers operational webhooks (notifications about server events), a Redis dead-letter queue with a redrive endpoint, OpenTelemetry export, and an SSRF guard that blocks internal IPs unless listed in whitelist_subnets. Client libraries for many languages and an npm-published CLI are referenced in the README.
use_cases: Sending webhooks to customers from an API product
Signing outgoing webhook payloads with HMAC or ed25519
Retrying and monitoring failed webhook deliveries
Notifying external systems of server events via operational webhooks
notable: Symmetric signatures by default, with asymmetric ed25519 keys available per endpoint
Operational webhooks that notify you about server events, using Svix itself
Redis-backed task queue with a managed dead-letter queue and redrive endpoint
Client libraries for Go, Python, JavaScript/TypeScript, Java, Kotlin, Ruby, C#, Rust, PHP, and Terraform
SSRF protection that blocks internal IP destinations by default
caveats: The README says only PostgreSQL is currently supported as a database
Some features of the hosted Svix service are not available in this open-source version
Redis is optional, but if used it needs persistence and a noeviction-style eviction policy
